question.problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-5=0 \\ 2x-y+z+1=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $x+2y-5=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,2,0⟩.$

- For the plane $2x-y+z+1=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨2,-1,1⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨1,2,0⟩\times ⟨2,-1,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2i-j-5k \\  & =⟨2,-1,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$
